Hardest scheme for greedy: degree. Weighted greedy + RR has a mean gap of 9.94% under degree weights (classes and n = 20, 50, 100, 200 pooled), against 6.36% (mixed), 3.26% (random), 2.79% (inverse). Ours + RR: 6.81% (degree), 4.87% (mixed), 3.28% (random), 3.26% (inverse).

Where ours gains most: BA / degree (6.39 ± 1.10% vs greedy + RR 12.56%); ER / degree (7.84 ± 1.94% vs greedy + RR 11.55%); Chordal / degree (4.16 ± 0.71% vs greedy + RR 7.30%). Ours + RR has the lower mean gap in 9 of 16 class × scheme cells.

Where greedy is better: in 7 of 16 cells weighted greedy + RR has the lower mean gap, under degree, inverse, random weights: Bipartite / inverse (3.72% vs 2.77%); BA / inverse (2.77% vs 2.15%); Bipartite / random (2.81% vs 2.32%); ER / inverse (5.69% vs 5.25%); ER / random (4.90% vs 4.54%); Bipartite / degree (9.13% vs 8.77%); BA / random (4.28% vs 4.17%). No mixed-scheme cell is among them.

Fine-tuning helped on the test grid: mean gap of the copied wtds model + RR 6.02 ± 0.98% → fine-tuned ours + RR 4.51 ± 0.89% (weighted greedy + RR 5.51%). With the same 1 s local search, ours + RR + LS reaches 2.24 ± 0.36% and greedy + RR + LS 2.76%.

Runtime: at n = 200 ours + RR takes 0.162 s per instance on the GPU, the ILP 3.54 s on average (30 s limit), weighted greedy + RR 0.9 ms. 16 of 640 ILP runs were not proven within 30 s (11 of them on ER graphs); they are excluded from the gaps.

n = 500 (no ILP): ours + RR is cheaper than weighted greedy + RR in 7 of 16 class × scheme cells. Under degree weights the difference in mean W(S) is -5.86% (ER), -2.91% (BA), +0.01% (Chordal), -2.67% (Bipartite) (negative = ours cheaper).
